sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Lesson 8.5 of Dataset Fundamentals: Version Control Fundamentals for Data. Traditional software version control was built for kilobyte text diffs. When applied naively to gigabyte parquet files or multi-terabyte imagery, standard Git breaks down with repository bloat, binary merge failures, and computational irreproducibility.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Today we decouple the lightweight cryptographic Control Plane versioned in Git from the immutable Data Plane in Content-Addressable Object Storage, unifying SHA-256 mappings, Merkle DAGs, logarithmic audit paths, deduplication scaling laws, and Semantic Versioning state transitions.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Modern data version control fundamentally separates the lightweight metadata Control Plane from the massive binary Data Plane.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Follow the three tiers left to right: in the Data Science Workspace, code and small pointer files like dataset dot dvc live alongside local reflink or hardlink caches. The Control Plane commits these pointers into Git, locking the exact SHA-256 Merkle root. The Data Plane stores the actual immutable blobs in cloud object storage like S3 or GCS, synchronizing only on demand!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Definition 8.5.1 establishes the foundation of Content-Addressable Storage: an arbitrary binary payload B is addressed strictly by its cryptographic digest h produced by a collision-resistant hash function like SHA-256.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: This hash satisfies three mandatory cryptographic guarantees: First, Pre-image resistance: finding the original payload given a digest requires 2 to the 256th operations. Second, Second pre-image resistance: finding another payload with the same digest requires 2 to the 256th operations. Third, Collision resistance: by the Birthday Paradox, finding any arbitrary pair of colliding payloads requires 2 to the 128th operations. The collision probability is strictly under 2 to the minus 128th—effectively zero in modern physics!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: To organize thousands of individual files into a tamper-evident repository, Definition 8.5.2 formulates the Merkle Directed Acyclic Graph over commits, directory trees, and file blobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: At the leaves, raw file blobs are hashed directly. A directory tree node hashes the sorted concatenation of its entry permissions, filenames, and child hashes. Finally, a commit node binds the root tree hash, author metadata, timestamp, and parent commit hash. By induction, changing even a single byte in any leaf blob triggers a cryptographic avalanche effect, flipping roughly 50 percent of the bits at the commit root!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: How can an edge device or audit client verify that a specific chunk belongs to a multi-terabyte dataset without downloading the whole corpus? Definition 8.5.3 formalizes the Merkle Audit Path.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: For a dataset partitioned into N chunks, a verifier needs only the target chunk itself and its Merkle Audit Path: a list of exactly d equals log base 2 of N sibling hashes along the path from leaf to root. Verification takes order log 2 of N time, and the bandwidth transferred is just the chunk plus d times 32 bytes—eliminating over 99.999 percent of network transfer!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: A dataset directory contains three partitions: part 0, part 1, and part 2 with directory root h root equals hash of h1, h2, h3. An engineer modifies a single scalar float in row 4,912 of part 1. Which blob hashes change, does h root change, and why can't an adversary forge a malicious row? Choose Option A, B, or C below me!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: How much physical storage does Content-Addressable deduplication actually save across multiple project releases? Definition 8.5.4 establishes the scaling laws.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: For a dataset with baseline size S 0 evolving across K releases with average mutation fraction delta, naive snapshots scale linearly as K times S 0. CAS stores the baseline once plus incremental churn, scaling as S 0 times 1 plus K minus 1 times delta. The deduplication savings ratio rho dedup is 1 minus 1 over K times 1 minus delta, converging asymptotically to 1 minus delta. At 5 percent churn, deduplication captures 95 percent storage savings!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: To prevent downstream machine learning pipelines from crashing, Definition 8.5.5 formalizes Semantic Versioning state transitions for datasets as an integer triplet M, m, p.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: A Major bump increments M and resets minor and patch to zero whenever there is a breaking schema change—like column deletion or attribute rename—or a label distribution shift that invalidates trained models. A Minor bump increments m whenever backwards-compatible features or additional sample batches are appended. A Patch bump increments p for typo corrections, corrupted entry repairs, or metadata errata fixes with zero structural alterations!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Two massive real-world projects demonstrate why Content-Addressable Storage is mandatory in modern AI engineering.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: First, Motional's nuScenes autonomous driving dataset captures 1.4 million camera frames and 400,000 LiDAR point clouds across 1,000 scenes, totaling over 500 gigabytes. Storing point clouds directly in standard Git crashed clones with fatal out-of-memory errors. Motional adopted a hybrid CAS architecture where Git tracks lightweight JSON annotation tables while immutable LiDAR arrays reside in S3, enabling millisecond branch switching. Second, during training of the 176-billion parameter BLOOM model, the BigScience workshop hashed 50-gigabyte text shards, saving over 60 percent in trans-European cloud network bandwidth!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In enterprise ML engineering, how do tools like Git-LFS, DVC, and Delta Lake fit together into a unified data versioning pipeline?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Git-LFS uses standard HTTP pointer protocols for medium binaries. DVC provides advanced data pipelines with multi-cloud remotes and DAG execution caching. Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg version columnar parquet files using ACID transaction logs. Underneath all of them, modern filesystems use copy-on-write reflinks to eliminate duplicate disk usage locally!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Slide 15 presents the executable Python verification suite from Section 8.5: GitLFSPointer, MerkleTreeNode, and CASStorageEngine built with Pydantic V2.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Notice how format_pointer_file produces the standard 3-line Git-LFS text. The commit_version method computes deterministic Merkle roots and stores unique SHA-256 digests in the blob pool. Look at the verified assertions: mutating labels changes the root hash while features and embeddings retain identical OIDs, deduplication captures 45 percent savings across two releases, and verify_merkle_audit_path verifies authentic chunks in logarithmic time while rejecting tampered payloads!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: To conclude Lesson 8.5, remember the Four Cardinal Rules of Data Version Control.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: First, always decouple the Control Plane from the Data Plane by committing lightweight pointer files in Git while storing binary payloads in Content-Addressable Object Storage. Second, rely on Merkle DAG avalanche hashing to verify integrity and detect tampering. Third, leverage block-level deduplication to capture up to 95 percent storage savings. Fourth, strictly enforce Semantic Versioning rules so breaking schema changes never crash downstream models. Next up in Lesson 8.6, we explore Version Control Tools: DVC, remote cloud remotes, and pipeline automation!
